The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. When sunlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it is made up of different wavelengths of light, including ultraviolet, visible light, and infrared. The shorter wavelengths, such as ultraviolet and visible light, are scattered more easily by the molecules in the atmosphere than the longer wavelengths.
